amendment_history.note: الإصدار الأصلي (22 مادة)، بموجب قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (416) وتاريخ 25/7/1442هـ. يحل محل نظام المحاسبين القانونيين الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/12) وتاريخ 13/5/1412هـ (مادة 21 من هذا النظام).

عدّل المواد (الأولى) و(الرابعة) و(الخامسة) و(التاسعة عشرة) و(العشرون)، ناقلاً صلاحيات إصدار وإلغاء التراخيص وتسمية موظفي الضبط من الوزارة/الوزير إلى الهيئة/المجلس. مسبوق بقرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (571) وتاريخ 5/8/1446هـ. نُشر ونُفذ وفق المصادر الثانوية المفحوصة هذا المسار (qanoonsa.com)؛ صفحة هيئة الخبراء المؤرشفة (Wayback 20251015113239) تعكس هذا التعديل عبر شارة 'changed-article' ونافذة تعديلات المادة فقط، لا عبر نص المادة الرئيسي المعروض (انظر known_unresolved_discrepancies، المفتاح accounting_auditing_boe_main_body_stale_vs_changelog_popup).

عدّل تعريف "الوزير" في المادة (الأولى) من "وزير التجارة" إلى تعريف عام (وزير من أعضاء مجلس الوزراء يسمى بأمر من رئيس مجلس الوزراء بناءً على اقتراح من مجلس الشؤون الاقتصادية والتنمية). نُشر في جريدة أم القرى، العدد 5118 وتاريخ 31/10/2025م، وفق qanoonsa.com. لاحق لأحدث لقطة أرشيفية متاحة لصفحة هيئة الخبراء هذا المسار (15 أكتوبر 2025)، فلا تعكسها هذه الصفحة إطلاقًا؛ اعتُمد بدلًا من ذلك على نسخة الهيئة السعودية للمراجعين والمحاسبين الرسمية (PDF) وقانونسا كمصدرين مستقلين (انظر known_unresolved_discrepancies، المفتاح accounting_auditing_cr283_not_yet_reflected_on_boe).

chapter_structure.label_ar: بدون تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول
chapter_structure.title_ar: مواد متسلسلة غير مجمعة تحت أبواب أو فصول رسمية، لا يحمل أي منها عنوانًا فرعيًا في المصدر (بخلاف بعض مسارات هذا المستودع الأخرى): تعريفات (م1) — حظر مزاولة المهنة دون ترخيص (م2) — ضوابط ترخيص المتفرغ وغير المتفرغ (م3) — إجراءات طلب الترخيص والبت فيه (م4) — إلغاء الترخيص (م5) — المقر الرئيس والفروع (م6) — التزامات المحاسب القانوني (م7) — محظورات المحاسب القانوني (م8) — أحكام التوقف عن مزاولة المهنة (م9) — الجرائم الجزائية وعقوباتها (م10) — اختصاص النيابة العامة (م11) — اختصاص القضاء بدعاوى التعويض (م12) — تشكيل لجنة النظر في المخالفات (م13) — اختصاص اللجنة بالمخالفات الإدارية والمسلكية (م14) — عقوبات اللجنة (م15) — التدابير التقويمية (م16) — سلطة المنع الاحترازي (م17) — استدعاء المخالف وإحالته للنيابة العامة (م18) — إعادة الترخيص بعد الشطب (م19) — موظفو الضبط (م20) — إحلال النظام محل نظام المحاسبين القانونيين (م21) — النفاذ وإصدار اللائحة (م22).

verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: laws.boe.gov.sa's LIVE portal was unreachable this pass (direct HTTPS curl to the exact law-detail URL [https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/6435e205-a7ae-4a8c-9580-ad0000b6bef2/1] returned curl exit code 000/no response; plain http:// returned HTTP 503), consistent with this corpus's established pattern for this BOE portal. archive.org/wayback/available confirmed a Wayback Machine snapshot of this exact BOE law-detail page at timestamp 20251015113239 (15 Oct 2025, HTTP 200, 17293 bytes), used as this track's PRIMARY source. The archived page was parsed with BeautifulSoup (not naive regex/tag-stripping): each of 22 'article_item' divs carries an 'h3.center' heading (bare ordinal, e.g. 'المادة الأولى', with NO inline topic title after it -- unlike the gcc_anti_dumping_law track's source page, this law's BOE HTML provides no per-article title text at all, for any of the 22 articles) and a 'div.HTMLContainer' body (article text,
tags converted to newlines). Five of the 22 'article_item' divs (Articles 1, 4, 5, 19, 20) additionally carry the class 'changed-article' and a nested 'تعديلات المادة' ('article amendments') popup quoting the Royal Decree M/169 (10/8/1446H, ~9 Feb 2025G) amendment text verbatim, introduced by the phrase 'لتصبح بالنص الآتي' ('to become the following text'). This exactly matches, article-for-article, the 5 articles independently reported as amended by qanoonsa.com's two separate pages summarizing Council of Ministers Resolution No. 571 (5/8/1446H) and Royal Decree M/169 (10/8/1446H) -- both fetched live this pass -- which describe the same substantive change (transferring licensing/registration authority from the Ministry of Commerce, 'الوزارة', to the Authority/SOCPA itself, 'الهيئة') for Articles 1, 4, 5, 19 and 20. CRITICAL VERIFIED ANOMALY -- BOE'S OWN PAGE INTERNALLY DISAGREES WITH ITSELF: for all 5 'changed-article'-flagged articles, the MAIN body text displayed on this same archived BOE page (i.e. what would render as the 'current' article text to an ordinary site visitor) still shows the OLDER, PRE-M/169 wording (e.g. Article 1's main body still lists a 'الوزارة: وزارة التجارة' definition, which M/169's own changelog popup says was DELETED; Article 1's 'الترخيص' definition in the main body still reads 'وثيقة تصدر من الوزارة' even though the changelog popup quotes the amended wording as 'وثيقة تصدر من الهيئة'). This was confirmed by comparing three snapshots of the identical URL: 20250119094540 (pre-M/169, no 'changed-article' classes at all, 16482 bytes), 20250513162018 (3 months after M/169's gazette publication, STILL no 'changed-article' classes, 16484 bytes), and 20251015113239 (8 months after, NOW showing 'changed-article' classes and changelog popups on the correct 5 articles, but 17293 bytes -- the size increase is attributable to the added changelog-popup markup, not to any correction of the main body text, which -- spot-checked verbatim -- is byte-identical to the pre-amendment copy). In other words: BOE's backend appears to have updated this law's per-article 'amendment metadata' (flags + changelog quotations) roughly 8 months after M/169's gazette publication, WITHOUT ever correspondingly refreshing the main displayed article body text for the same 5 articles, in any of the 3 Wayback snapshots checked this pass (spanning Jan-Oct 2025). No Wayback snapshot after 20251015113239 exists (CDX query returned empty for the period 16 Oct 2025 -- 18 Jul 2026), and the live portal is unreachable, so it could not be confirmed this pass whether BOE's main body text has since been corrected. RESOLUTION TAKEN THIS PASS: this track ingests the AMENDED wording (i.e. BOE's own changelog-popup text, NOT BOE's stale main body text) as the current, in-force text of Articles 1, 4, 5, 19 and 20, because: (a) the changelog-popup text is itself BOE-hosted primary-source content directly quoting Royal Decree M/169 ('لتصبح بالنص الآتي: ...'), not a third-party paraphrase; (b) it is independently, word-for-word corroborated by SOCPA's own official PDF of the law (socpa.org.sa, the profession's own regulator and administering authority under this exact law -- see SECONDARY CROSS-VERIFICATION below); and (c) it is further corroborated by two independent qanoonsa.com pages summarizing Council of Ministers Resolution 571 and Royal Decree M/169 with matching article numbers and substance. Using BOE's demonstrably stale main-body wording as this track's 'current' text would risk exactly the kind of unverified/outdated-text risk this corpus's trust policy forbids, given multiply-corroborated evidence that it no longer reflects the law actually in force. This stale-main-body anomaly is recorded as a named discrepancy (accounting_auditing_boe_main_body_stale_vs_changelog_popup) rather than silently resolved. SECONDARY CROSS-VERIFICATION (near-complete, independent regulator source): SOCPA (الهيئة السعودية للمراجعين والمحاسبين -- the very authority this law establishes/licenses under) hosts its own official PDF of the complete 22-article law text at socpa.org.sa/SOCPA/files/06/066109b0-5a63-47b6-8fd5-10546e7ca91b.pdf (direct fetch to socpa.org.sa returned curl exit 35 / connection reset this pass; fetched instead via a Wayback Machine snapshot dated 20260116022237, HTTP 200, 848373 bytes, 12-page PDF, extracted with pdftotext -layout). This PDF -- despite being filed/labelled '1442هـ - 2021م' (the year of original enactment) -- shows CURRENT, POST-AMENDMENT wording throughout: it matches BOE's stale-main-body text (byte-for-byte, modulo PDF bidi-reordering artifacts and Arabic-numeral-vs-hamza spacing noise from pdftotext extraction) for all 17 unamended articles, AND matches BOE's own changelog-popup wording (not BOE's stale main body) for Articles 4, 5, 19 and 20 verbatim. This is strong, independent, near-full-text cross-verification from the regulator's own published copy of the law it itself administers. A FURTHER, SECOND, MORE RECENT AMENDMENT TO ARTICLE 1 (Council of Ministers Resolution 283, 22/4/1447H / 14 Oct 2025G, published Umm Al-Qura Gazette Issue 5118 dated 31/10/2025G, per qanoonsa.com, fetched live this pass) further amended Article 1's 'الوزير' ('the Minister') definition -- generalizing it from 'وزير التجارة' (Minister of Commerce) to 'وزير من أعضاء مجلس الوزراء يسمى بأمر من رئيس مجلس الوزراء بناءً على اقتراح من مجلس الشؤون الاقتصادية والتنمية' (a minister among Council of Ministers members, designated by Prime Ministerial order upon the proposal of the Council of Economic and Development Affairs). This amendment POST-DATES this track's only available BOE Wayback snapshot (20251015113239, 15 Oct 2025 -- captured just before Resolution 283's 31 Oct 2025 gazette publication), so BOE's own archived page shows ZERO trace of it (no 'changed-article' flag or changelog-popup addition covering it) -- consistent with a timing gap, not a source disagreement. This track nonetheless incorporates Resolution 283's change into Article 1's ingested current text, sourced from: (i) SOCPA's own currently-published PDF (fetched via the 16 Jan 2026 Wayback snapshot, i.e. after Resolution 283), which shows exactly this generalized 'الوزير' wording; and (ii) qanoonsa.com's independent citation of Resolution 283's number, date, gazette issue, and exact new wording (word-for-word match with SOCPA's PDF). No separate Royal Decree number was found ratifying Resolution 283 specifically (unlike the M/169/CoM-Resolution-571 pair, where a Royal Decree explicitly accompanied and ratified the Council of Ministers Resolution) -- this is flagged as an open sourcing question, not resolved as a settled negative finding; see known_unresolved_discrepancies. PREDECESSOR LAW -- CONFIRMED, CLEAN SUPERSESSION (unlike the more ambiguous gcc_anti_dumping_law M/7 case): this law's own Article 21 explicitly states: 'يحل النظام محل نظام المحاسبين القانونيين، الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/12) وتاريخ 13/5/1412هـ، ويلغي كل ما يتعارض معه من أحكام' ('This Law replaces the Law of Certified Public Accountants, issued by Royal Decree No. M/12 dated 13/5/1412H, and repeals whatever conflicts with it'). This was independently, directly confirmed by fetching BOE's own separate law-detail page for 'نظام المحاسبين القانونيين' (lawId 56195fdf-46c2-44f0-88e5-a9a700f1be50, via Wayback snapshot 20251116125030, 16 Nov 2025, HTTP 200): that page's own metadata shows decree 'مرسوم ملكي رقم م/12 بتاريخ 13/5/1412هـ' (19/11/1991G), Council of Ministers Resolution 40 dated 12/5/1412H, and -- critically -- its own 'الحالة' (status) field reads 'لاغي' (VOID/repealed), not 'ساري'. This track therefore does NOT ingest M/12's articles (only the current, in-force M/59 text is ingested, per this corpus's standard practice); M/12 is documented here purely as confirmed historical/superseded context, per this corpus's copyright_law/telecommunications_law precedent for confirmed supersessions. COMPANION INSTRUMENTS EXPLICITLY DISTINGUISHED, NOT CONFLATED: the same Council of Ministers Resolution 416 (25/7/1442H) that approved this Law ALSO, in the SAME resolution, (a) renamed SOCPA from 'الهيئة السعودية للمحاسبين القانونيين' to 'الهيئة السعودية للمراجعين والمحاسبين', and (b) separately approved 'تنظيم الهيئة السعودية للمراجعين والمحاسبين' (SOCPA's own organizational statute/regulation -- confirmed to exist as a SEPARATE BOE-catalogued instrument, lawId 3fd2d5d4-e39f-4543-a69f-ad0100b32c4d, found via web search this pass but NOT fetched/ingested). Per this track's task brief, this is explicitly NOT the same law as the one ingested here: this track covers ONLY the profession-practice law (نظام مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة -- licensing, professional conduct, and disciplinary provisions for accountants/auditors), not SOCPA's own establishing/organizational statute. IMPLEMENTING REGULATION: confirmed to exist (اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة -- referenced throughout the ingested articles, e.g. Articles 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 15, 22; hosted by qanoniah.com per a web search this pass, and itself reportedly amended in 2025 per istitlaa.ncc.gov.sa and alweeam.com search results). Consistent with this corpus's established precedent (finance_lease_law, banking_control_law, insurance_control_law, finance_companies_law, cooperative_health_insurance_law, healthcare_professions_law, gcc_anti_dumping_law), this track ingests ONLY the primary Law; the Implementing Regulation is flagged as a follow-up candidate, not fabricated or partially guessed at. TITLE NAMING NUANCE: BOE's own canonical title for this law is 'نظام مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة' (NO 'مزاولة'). This track's own initial task brief and this corpus's coverage_gap_map.json entry both gloss the law as 'نظام مزاولة مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة' / 'نظام مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة' -- BOE's verified title omits the word 'مزاولة' (which does appear repeatedly WITHIN the law's articles, e.g. Article 2: 'لا تجوز مزاولة المهنة إلا بعد الحصول على الترخيص', but not in the law's own official title). This track uses BOE's exact verified title. STRUCTURE: this Law is NOT subdivided into أبواب (parts) or فصول (chapters) -- it is a flat sequence of 22 articles, none of which carries an inline BOE-sourced title (unlike gcc_anti_dumping_law's source page, which supplied an inline title for 16 of its 17 articles). No title_ar field is fabricated for any article; consistent with this corpus's finance_lease_law precedent (whose BOE source similarly supplies no inline per-article titles), this track's articles carry no title_ar key at all, relying on section_ar for structural context. GAP-MAP ESTIMATE CORRECTED: this corpus's own reports/coverage_gap_map/coverage_gap_map.json entry for this law stated 'estimated_article_count: Not confirmed — needs verification' and 'estimated_decree: Royal Decree, replacing the 1412H Certified Public Accountants Law; exact current decree number/date not confirmed in this pass'. This pass confirms: Royal Decree M/59 dated 27/7/1442H (11/3/2021G), 22 articles, subsequently amended by Royal Decree M/169 (10/8/1446H) and Council of Ministers Resolution 283 (22/4/1447H); predecessor confirmed as Royal Decree M/12 dated 13/5/1412H (status 'لاغي' on BOE). No legal text is altered beyond whitespace normalization (collapsing repeated spaces, converting
tags to newlines, and -- for the 5 amended articles only -- reconstructing clean Unicode Arabic from BOE's own changelog-popup wording, cross-checked word-for-word against SOCPA's PDF, in place of pdftotext's bidi-reordered extraction). Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation performed on the Arabic text (English descriptions in this note and in document_en/issuing_authority_en are for indexing only). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: This track's single most important documented discrepancy. BOE's own archived law-detail page (Wayback snapshot 20251015113239, 15 Oct 2025) marks Articles 1, 4, 5, 19 and 20 with a 'changed-article' CSS class and a nested 'تعديلات المادة' changelog popup that directly quotes Royal Decree M/169's (10/8/1446H) amended wording -- yet the SAME page's main, primarily-displayed article body text for those exact same 5 articles still shows the OLDER, pre-M/169 wording (verified by diffing three snapshots: 20250119094540 pre-M/169, 20250513162018 three months after M/169's gazette publication, and 20251015113239 eight months after -- the main body text is byte-identical across all three; only the changelog-popup markup was added between the second and third snapshot). This track resolves this by ingesting the changelog-popup (post-M/169) wording, not the stale main body, as the current in-force text -- corroborated word-for-word by SOCPA's own official PDF of the law and by two independent qanoonsa.com pages describing the same amendments. No Wayback snapshot after 15 Oct 2025 exists to confirm whether BOE's main body has since been corrected, and the live BOE portal was unreachable this pass (curl exit 000 over HTTPS, HTTP 503 over HTTP). BOE's own main-body article text for these 5 articles is confirmed genuinely stale relative to the current, amended law -- not a proxy or reachability artifact -- since the same byte-identical old wording persisted across three snapshots spanning 8+ months after the amending decree's own gazette publication.

Article 1's 'الوزير' (Minister) definition was further amended by Council of Ministers Resolution No. 283 dated 22/4/1447H (14 Oct 2025G), published Umm Al-Qura Gazette Issue 5118 dated 31/10/2025G (per qanoonsa.com, fetched live this pass), generalizing it from 'وزير التجارة' (Minister of Commerce) to 'وزير من أعضاء مجلس الوزراء يسمى بأمر من رئيس مجلس الوزراء بناءً على اقتراح من مجلس الشؤون الاقتصادية والتنمية'. This track's only available BOE Wayback snapshot (20251015113239, 15 Oct 2025) predates Resolution 283's gazette publication by roughly two weeks, so it shows zero trace of this change -- a timing gap, not a source disagreement. This track incorporates Resolution 283's wording into Article 1's ingested current text, sourced from SOCPA's own currently-published PDF of the law (fetched via a 16 Jan 2026 Wayback snapshot, i.e. after Resolution 283) and independently cross-checked against qanoonsa.com's citation of the resolution's number, date, gazette issue, and exact wording. UNRESOLVED: no separate Royal Decree number was found specifically ratifying Resolution 283 (unlike the M/169 / Council of Ministers Resolution 571 pair, where a Royal Decree explicitly accompanied and ratified the Council of Ministers Resolution) -- it remains an open question whether such a Royal Decree exists but was not surfaced by the secondary sources available this pass, or whether this specific administrative-definition tweak was validly actioned by Council of Ministers Resolution alone. A future pass with direct access to Umm Al-Qura Gazette Issue 5118 (31/10/2025G) or a working live BOE fetch (post-dating this amendment) could resolve this decisively.

laws.boe.gov.sa's LIVE portal returned curl exit code 000 (no response) over HTTPS and HTTP 503 over plain HTTP for this law's exact detail URL, repeated attempts, this pass -- consistent with this corpus's established pattern for this BOE portal (see e.g. gcc_anti_dumping_law, finance_lease_law). A single Wayback Machine snapshot of the identical URL (20251015113239, 15 Oct 2025, HTTP 200, 17293 bytes) was reachable and used as this track's primary source; no later snapshot exists (CDX query for the period 16 Oct 2025 -- 18 Jul 2026 returned empty). socpa.org.sa was also directly unreachable this pass (curl exit 35 / connection reset over HTTPS); its official PDF was likewise recovered only via a Wayback Machine snapshot (20260116022237).

Unlike gcc_anti_dumping_law's BOE source page (which supplies an inline topic title after a colon in 16 of 17 article headings), this law's BOE-hosted HTML supplies NO inline title text for any of its 22 articles -- every 'h3.center' heading is a bare ordinal (e.g. 'المادة الأولى') with nothing following it. Consistent with this corpus's finance_lease_law precedent (whose BOE source similarly lacks inline per-article titles), this track's articles carry no title_ar key at all rather than a fabricated one; section_ar is used for structural/topical context instead.

This law has NO أبواب (parts) or فصول (chapters) -- it is a flat sequence of 22 individually-numbered articles with no grouping/part headers anywhere on the BOE page (no chapter-level HTML elements were found alongside the 22 'article_item' divs). This track's chapter_structure field reflects this verified flat structure (a single leaf range 1-22) rather than inventing a topical grouping not present in the primary source.

BOE's own canonical title for this law is 'نظام مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة' -- WITHOUT the word 'مزاولة' ('practice/exercise of'). This track's own initial task brief referred to the law as 'نظام مزاولة مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة', and this corpus's own coverage_gap_map.json entry uses 'نظام مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة' (matching BOE). 'مزاولة' does appear repeatedly within the law's own article bodies (e.g. Article 2: 'لا تجوز مزاولة المهنة إلا بعد الحصول على الترخيص') but not in the law's own official title as catalogued by BOE. This track uses BOE's exact verified title ('document' field) and records this naming nuance here rather than silently reconciling it.

The Law's companion Implementing Regulation (اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة) is confirmed to exist -- referenced throughout the ingested articles (e.g. Articles 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 15, 22) and independently found hosted at qanoniah.com, with a further 2025 amendment to it reported via istitlaa.ncc.gov.sa and alweeam.com (both found via web search this pass, neither fetched in full). Consistent with this corpus's established precedent (finance_lease_law, banking_control_law, insurance_control_law, finance_companies_law, cooperative_health_insurance_law, healthcare_professions_law, gcc_anti_dumping_law), this track ingests ONLY the primary Law. The Implementing Regulation -- including whatever amendment history attaches to it independently of the two Law-level amendments documented here -- is documented here as a candidate for a dedicated follow-up ingestion pass, not fabricated or partially guessed at.

The same Council of Ministers Resolution (416, 25/7/1442H) that approved this Law also, in the same resolution, separately approved 'تنظيم الهيئة السعودية للمراجعين والمحاسبين' (SOCPA's own organizational statute/regulation -- confirmed via web search this pass to be a SEPARATE BOE-catalogued instrument, lawId 3fd2d5d4-e39f-4543-a69f-ad0100b32c4d, NOT fetched or ingested this pass) and renamed the Authority from 'الهيئة السعودية للمحاسبين القانونيين' to 'الهيئة السعودية للمراجعين والمحاسبين'. Per this track's task brief, this organizational statute governs SOCPA's own institutional structure/governance and is explicitly distinct from -- and must not be conflated with -- the profession-practice law (licensing, professional conduct, and disciplinary provisions for accountants/auditors) ingested in this track.
